findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, allowing denials to leak between identities
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built only from namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent folder. validateSubject permits multiple identity types, and different identities can have the same identifier string. For example, 'anonymous:0' and 'render:0' both parse to userUID "0". If an anonymous check for 'dashboards:read' on a dashboard is denied, the denial is cached under a key like ns.perm_0_dashboards:read_<dash>_. A subsequent renderer check for the same dashboard will hit this denial cache at line 117 and be denied before getRendererPermissions can return its built-in read access. The denial cache key must include the identity type (and ideally a normalized internal identity ID) to avoid cross-identity wrongful denials.

findings.title: Cached denial can persist after permission is granted
findings.body: When a permission check reaches the database and denies access, the result is cached in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30 seconds). There is no invalidation when permissions change. If the first check for a newly created dashboard/folder happens before the new permission is visible (for example due to read-replica lag or asynchronous permission provisioning), the denial is cached. Subsequent checks within the TTL hit the denial cache and skip the database requery, leaving the creator unable to access the newly created resource for up to the TTL. This reintroduces the same class of staleness problem the PR is trying to fix.

findings.title: Denial cache key construction is ambiguous because fields are joined with underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent using '_' as a separator. Dashboard/folder UIDs can contain underscores, so different combinations of name and parent can produce identical cache keys. For example, name='a_b' with parent='c' yields the same key suffix as name='a' with parent='b_c'. Because this cache stores negative authorization decisions, a key collision can cause a denial for one resource/folder combination to be incorrectly applied to another resource. The key should be constructed with unambiguous escaping/encoding or by hashing the separate fields.

findings.title: Tests do not cover denial-cache isolation by identity type or grant-after-denial behavior
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck only pre-seeds a denial entry for a user and checks that it denies access. It does not verify that denial entries are scoped by identity type, so it would not catch a denial for anonymous affecting the renderer identity. It also does not verify behavior when a permission is granted after a denial has been cached. Since the denial cache is a new authorization decision path, tests should cover cross-identity isolation and stale-denial scenarios.
